text:
Claude Giroux played 1,000 games for the Flyers, and last week he was reminded how long ago some of them were. He now shares a dressing room with Tyler Boucher, son of his former Philadelphia teammate Brian Boucher, and TSN's headline caught Giroux's reaction: "It makes me feel old." The same night he scored against his old team in an overtime loss.

He's 38 and still useful in ways the box score undersells. At five-on-five the Senators take 61% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, far better than when he sits. His 13 points in 24 games lag that because Ottawa has scored 4.9 fewer goals than those chances deserved with him out there, and that usually swings back.

None of this is a surprise. Evolving-Hockey had him 2.1 wins above replacement last season, 47th among 401 forwards, and good at taking chances away too. His last ten games: three goals, including the winner against Pittsburgh on the night Linus Ullmark won his 200th. And the Hall of Fame talk has started; Broad Street Buzz ran a piece on a Hall of Famer who thinks he belongs.
headline: Claude Giroux, 38, is still tilting the ice
